guideTitle: The Best Tablet Stands Under $30 for Reading, Calls and a Second Screen
metaDescription: Low-cost aluminum tablet stands differ in device size range, load rating and how they adjust. We compared four on fit, stability features and folding.
introParagraphs: Around $30, tablet stands are almost all aluminum; the differences are how large a device they hold, whether they state a load rating, and how they adjust, from continuous joints to fixed tilt slots.
Check your device's size and weight first, especially if you plan to use a heavier 13-inch tablet or a portable monitor. Two stands here state a load rating (about 2.2 to 2.4 lb); the others don't.
Three of the four were under $30 at the time of writing; the Urmust was slightly over. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

best-tablet-stands-under-30-1.summary: An aluminum stand for 4.7- to 15.6-inch devices, rated to 2.42 lb, with adjustable joints and cable clips.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-1.description:
The Urmust offers the most adjustment and a stated load rating: 2.42 lb, for devices from 4.7 to 15.6 inches, with adjustable joints tightened by an included wrench and clips to route the charging cable.

It was slightly above $30 at the time of writing. Urmust describes a base designed for stability with heavier devices.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-1.bestFor: Larger tablets at a desk, where height and angle matter.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-1.skipIf: You want a stand to carry around; the slim foldable stand packs flat.

best-tablet-stands-under-30-2.summary: UGREEN's dual-rod aluminum stand for 4- to 13-inch devices, with silicone pads and rubber feet.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-2.description:
The UGREEN uses two support rods rather than one, a design intended to reduce wobble, with silicone padding to protect the device and rubber feet to stop sliding. It fits 4- to 13-inch devices and folds for storage.

It doesn't state a load rating, and 13 inches is its upper limit.
cons: Less height adjustment than the Urmust
best-tablet-stands-under-30-2.bestFor: Using a tablet as a steady second screen beside a laptop.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-2.skipIf: Your device is larger than 13 inches; the Bimo goes to 16.

best-tablet-stands-under-30-3.summary: Bimo's 360-degree rotating aluminum stand for 4- to 16-inch devices, rated to 1kg.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-3.description:
The Bimo covers the largest devices here, up to 16 inches, with a stated 1kg (2.2 lb) load rating, which makes it suitable for many portable monitors as well as tablets. It rotates 360 degrees.

A full-coverage non-slip foam base helps it stay put, and it folds as one piece. Check your monitor's weight against the rating.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-3.skipIf: You need more height; the Urmust's jointed arm adjusts further.

best-tablet-stands-under-30-4.summary: A slim foldable aluminum stand for 7- to 13-inch devices with 8 fixed tilt slots.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-4.description:
This slim stand uses 8 fixed tilt slots rather than a continuous hinge, so each angle locks in place, and it supports portrait or landscape orientation. It fits 7- to 13-inch devices, has silicone grips and folds flat.

It was the lowest-priced stand here at the time of writing, and it doesn't state a load rating.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-4.bestFor: Reading, recipes and video calls, at home or on the move.
best-tablet-stands-under-30-4.skipIf: You need eye-level height; the Urmust raises the device.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Check the size range and, where stated, load rating: Urmust 2.42 lb, Bimo 1kg.
Jointed arms (Urmust) raise and angle; slot stands (the slim foldable) lock fixed angles.
Rubber feet, foam bases and silicone pads help stability and protect the device.
The UGREEN, Bimo and slim stand fold.

faq.a: All four list 13 inches or more; check weight against the Urmust's or Bimo's rating.

faq.q: Can I use a portable monitor?
faq.a: The Bimo is designed for it, within its 1kg rating.
Slots lock set angles; joints give continuous adjustment but may need tightening.
The UGREEN, Bimo and slim stand fold; the Urmust is a desk stand.

faq.q: Can I charge while it's on the stand?
faq.a: Yes; the Urmust includes cable clips to route the cable.

bottomLine: For a desk, the Urmust offers the most adjustment and a stated load rating, just over $30; the UGREEN's dual rods are the steadier simple option.
For portable monitors, the Bimo covers up to 16 inches, and for travel or reading, the slim foldable stand is the lowest-cost pick.
